collections/enumeration#

Adds a stable integer index to every item of an Iterating object.

Version: v1.0.0

Synopsis#

let cursor = Enumerated(origin: names).cursor();
let first = cursor.item();
// first.index() == 0
// first.item() is the first name

Description#

Adds a stable integer index to every item of an Iterating object.

Enumerated does not consume or change the origin. Its cursor is immutable: successor() returns another cursor while the previous cursor keeps pointing at the same indexed item.

Number values from zero:

Number values from a chosen index, for example human-friendly line numbers:

let lines = Enumerated(origin: document.lines(), start: 1);
let output = Stdout();
for lines -> line {
    output.writeln(line.index().string(), ": ", line.item());
}

Each line received by the loop is an Indexed<string>. Its index() is the line number and its item() is the original line.

Advance without mutation:

let first = Enumerated(origin: names).cursor();
let second = first.successor();
// first.item().index() == 0
// second.item().index() == 1

Check available() before item() or successor(). Calling either method on an exhausted cursor throws IterationEnded. If another item would require an index larger than int.max, successor() throws EnumerationOverflow.
